item.text: I’m checking the current source again to find the next refactor that actually improves structure rather than just renaming things. At this point the meaningful target is separation of concerns and making the sort implementation less tightly coupled to one in-place flow.

I found a concrete improvement: `sortedCopy` currently re-validates through `sort`, and each digit pass allocates fresh working arrays. I’m refactoring that into a single validated execution path with reusable buffers, and I’m separating the demo entry point from the utility class.
The core refactor is in. I’m adding a separate demo class now so `RadixSort` stays a pure library type instead of also owning the example runtime entry point.
I’ve separated the reusable code from the demo. Next I’m compiling both classes and running the demo to verify the new flow, including the non-mutating `sortedCopy` path.

Refactored the code into a cleaner library/demo split.

[RadixSort.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/038_radix_sort/RadixSort.java:1) is now just the reusable sorting utility. I removed the embedded `main`, introduced a single internal `sortValidated(...)` path so `sortedCopy(...)` no longer re-validates through `sort(...)`, and changed the implementation to reuse `output` and `counts` buffers across digit passes instead of reallocating them every iteration.

I also added [RadixSortDemo.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/038_radix_sort/RadixSortDemo.java:1) as a separate entry point. That keeps the utility class focused and demonstrates the non-mutating API by printing both the original array and the sorted copy.
